text:
morgan: quick heads-up — running into a generator streaming hang in the Go SDK when the auth token refreshes mid-stream. simple loop, then auth refresh from our infra, and the iterator never returns, goroutines pile up. anyone seen this?

anya: ugh. which SDK version? can you paste the tiny repro? usually plumbed contexts fix it but generator ergonomics sometimes don't propagate cancellation.

morgan: using v0.13.2. minimal pattern:
```go
ctx := context.Background()
g := client.Generator(ctx, \"gpt-test\", opts)
it := g.Stream(ctx, input)
for it.Next() {
    token := it.Token()
    fmt.Print(token)
}
if err := it.Err(); err != nil {
    log.Printf(\"stream error: %v\", err)
}
```
Then our infra rotates credentials (auth refresh), server replies Unauthenticated and we see: iterator stalls (no Next() return), goroutine stacks show readLoop blocked on recv.

samir: saw similar in prod traces. tokens spike and 40+ goroutines stuck in generator.readLoop waiting for a close signal after grpc returns Unauthenticated. Workaround was to wrap stream iteration with a manual timeout ctx and cancel on auth refresh, but that feels brittle.

anya: can you share the stack trace? IIRC the read loop only closes on io.EOF or explicit stream.Close. If grpc error isn't propagated down to the iterator, Next() blocks.

morgan: attaching short log excerpt (sanitized):
```
rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = token expired
goroutine 1200 [chan receive]:
main.(*generator).readLoop(0xc0000...)
	/go/pkg/mod/.../generator.go:234 +0x123
```

jules: this is an ergonomics gap. two complementary things we could do: 1) make the iterator return immediately on non-retriable grpc errors (propagate error into it.Err()), 2) add a StreamHandle that owns cancel and a Close() method so callers can ensure cleanup without relying on ctx closure. Example API: `type StreamHandle interface { Next() bool; Token() string; Err() error; Close() }` — Close should force internal goroutine teardown.

samir: agree. also believe the auth-refresh path currently attempts a retry but the retry path rewraps channels and loses the consumer signal. A tiny patch where retry uses the same consumer channel (or forwards the error) fixed our repro locally. I'll push a prototype PR. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: created issue #4123: \"go-sdk: generator stream hang on auth refresh\" (morgan)

anya: if you can whip up a 20-line sampleapp that reliably reproduces this I'll prioritize it for the next sprint. devex can help minimize environment deps.

morgan: will do — I can also test samir's patch. thanks everyone, opening a compact repro now and will ping when it's up. :pray:

jules: one last thought — we should document recommended patterns for consumers: prefer passing a child ctx per-stream, and always select on ctx.Done() in your consuming loop as a defensive measure. but SDK should be resilient by default.

morgan: yep, adding that to the sample app + README. appreciate the quick triage!
